R1079.ai_methods_detail: unspecified machine learning regression surrogate trained on outputs of an in-house physics-based crop-PV model (algorithm not named in abstract)

R2039.justification: A UAV-photogrammetry 3D orchard model and a PV simulation engine sit in a CesiumJS interface that receives real-time sensor data automatically through Node-RED, MQTT and InfluxDB, so there is an automated data link into a virtual model. The bidirectional link was shown only by remote actuation of a physical solar tracker, and nothing says the model's outputs set the tracker automatically, so the closed-loop claim is the authors' term and this is coded as a shadow demonstrated on a testbed tracker.

R2082.ai_methods_detail: AI-assisted surrogate model (algorithm not named in abstract) combined with evolutionary multi-objective optimization producing Pareto-optimal solutions

R2176.justification: Edge and cloud data management feed real-time field observations into irrigation, panel-cleaning and tilt models that output operational recommendations for irrigation and PV operation, with no automatic actuation described. The platform was field-evaluated on a pilot-scale agrivoltaic field over the 2025 growing season, and its 'data-driven' irrigation module names no machine learning method.

R2458.ai_methods_detail: Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network for crop yield and energy prediction; multi-objective optimization (method not named)

R2492.ai_methods_detail: Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, SVR, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, SHAP interpretation, and a proposed SHAP-Guided Stacked Ensemble-LSTM (SG-SEL) hybrid

R0652.justification: The authors call it a digital-twin framework, but the abstract describes a geometric ray-tracing model and genomic (genetic-algorithm) optimization of greenhouse design, tested only on representative numerical examples with no data link to a real installation, so it is an offline design digital model with no ML.

R1231.ai_methods_detail: GRU (gated recurrent unit) hybridised with AdaBoost for classification of crop health and solar panel condition; cosine-similarity redundancy elimination for data aggregation
R1231.justification: The study describes an IoT wireless sensor network that classifies real-time data with a hybrid GRU-AdaBoost model (EeAVM) to monitor crop and panel condition, but it builds no virtual model of the agrivoltaic system, never uses the digital twin term, and does not say where the classifier runs.

R1367.ai_methods_detail: GWO-optimised BP (back-propagation) neural network for greenhouse temperature forecasting; APSO-optimised fuzzy PID temperature controller

R1134.justification: The authors propose a large-scale digital twin to predict crop yield under panel coverage, but the reported work is an ongoing shading experiment whose sensor network gathers data 'to build' the twin, with AI analytics only 'to be developed', so it is at most a conceptual digital model with no automated model link and no AI yet.

R1397.ai_methods_detail: CNN transfer learning with pre-trained EfficientNetV2L, EfficientNetV2M and ResNet50 (Keras) for chili crop counting and harvest prediction
R1397.justification: The study fine-tunes pre-trained CNNs offline to count chili crops and predict harvest in a solar-powered IoT greenhouse, adds a life cycle analysis, builds no virtual model of the agrivoltaic system, and does not use digital twin terminology.

R0886.justification: The abstract describes a 'digital replica' (not called a digital twin or shadow) that ray-traces light in a procedurally generated agrivoltaic system, feeds the daily radiation into a crop model, and uses a genomic (genetic) multi-objective optimization over 50 generations for design. The methods are physics-based simulation plus metaheuristic GA, with no ML. It is a design-stage simulation with no data link to a real installation, so it is a digital model run offline.

R0930.ai_methods_detail: Unspecified machine-learning model using panel-layout features to forecast shaded insolation (algorithm not named in abstract)
R0930.justification: The authors 'constructed a machine-learning model with panel layout features to forecast the insolation shaded by solar panels' and tested it 'as a simulation result'. The abstract does not name the ML family, so classical_ml is assumed. Layout optimization is mentioned only as a possible future use. No data link to a physical installation or DT term is described, so this is an offline digital model.

R0135.ai_methods_detail: Artificial neural network (ANN) predicting instantaneous electricity production of the PV greenhouse

The ANN was built from the monitoring data, but the abstract describes no automated live link between the model and the installation and does not use the DT term, so this is an offline digital model used for prediction.

R1762.ai_methods_detail: Unspecified 'artificial intelligence' in the cloud cyber domain for predictive analysis (algorithm not named in abstract; check full text)

Actuators and 'dynamic control' are mentioned only through the GUI, and the abstract never shows model outputs automatically setting actuators, so this is a shadow at most; it runs on a campus prototype, and the AI method is not named (ai_used provisional).

R1794.ai_methods_detail: Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM)
R1794.justification: The paper 'implements several Machine Learning models such as ANN, GPR, LR, DT, and SVM to predict the APV power generation' of a project in Gujarat and compares them by RMSE, MSE, MAE and R2. This is offline data-driven forecasting with no automated link to the installation and no DT term, so it is a digital model used for prediction.

R1443.ai_methods_detail: Unspecified machine learning and analytics module within a proposed AI-based decision support system, coupled with unspecified multi-objective optimization for louvre angle control (architecture only, not yet implemented)
R1443.justification: The proposed DSS 'integrates and synchronizes multi-sensor data acquisition, data quality management, machine learning and analytics, and multi-objective optimization for adaptive control of the louvre to a specified angle position' for real-time control, so as designed the model outputs automatically set the louvre actuator in a two-way loop. It is explicitly only 'a comprehensive architectural blueprint' with 'implementation and simulation ongoing', so it is a concept, and ML is part of the study's own proposed system rather than only cited.

R1618.justification: Soil moisture, crop status and environmental data are 'continuously monitored' over LoRaWAN and PLC links 'to assist climate-adaptive crop modeling' and irrigation scheduling, an automated data-to-model flow, but the abstract does not show the crop model's outputs automatically setting actuators; the nutrient module regulates fertilizer 'based on ... soil nutrient sensor readings and crop growth phases', which reads as sensor-driven control rather than model-driven actuation, so shadow at most. Performance is 'confirmed by MATLAB-based simulations and real-world practical case studies' with no named field installation, so prototype level (weakly evidenced), and only generic 'real-time data analytics' is named, with no ML method. Final check: performance is supported only by MATLAB simulations and unspecified case studies with no named installation, so the system is coded as not demonstrated.

R1638.ai_methods_detail: Conv1D and MaxPooling feature extraction with a modified spiking neural network (Adaptive Exponential Integrate-and-Fire, SNN-AdEx) classifier; Euclidean distance threshold for redundancy filtering; compared against MLEM, MLELMAKF, SOF-SVM and MRMR-KNN baselines
R1638.justification: EE-SAMS is a wireless sensor network data-aggregation framework that does node-level redundancy filtering and aggregator-level Conv1D plus SNN-AdEx classification (99.27% accuracy) before forwarding data to a base station, so it uses deep learning across a node, aggregator and base-station hierarchy; it has no virtual model of the agrivoltaic system and is aimed at 'real-time agrovoltaic monitoring'.

R1932.justification: The cloud platform ingests real-time environmental, agronomic and machine data and uses 'automation models that adjust fertigation schedules dynamically' by phenology, weather and soil, but no physics-based or data-driven model of crop, water or PV behavior is described, so this is monitoring plus scheduling logic and there is no virtual model to grade. The system was field-validated for LoRaWAN coverage and transmission reliability and used in field campaigns under agrivoltaic modules, so it runs on an operating installation, and no ML method is named.

R1950.ai_methods_detail: Recurrent neural networks (RNN) and directed spatio-temporal graph neural networks (STGNN) for predicting greenhouse internal temperature
R1950.justification: The study benchmarks RNNs against STGNNs on historical 15-minute datasets from a Volos PV greenhouse (STGNN R2 = 0.905 vs 0.740 on the 2024 data), which is an offline data-driven predictive model with no live data link; it presents itself only as 'a fast empirical core for real-time digital twins', not as a digital twin itself.

R2188.ai_methods_detail: Bayesian-optimization-tuned LSTM for day-ahead PV forecasting (six forecasting model families in 21 configurations compared); MILP for cost-minimizing scheduling
R2188.justification: The abstract describes a two-stage framework, a Bayesian-optimized LSTM day-ahead PV forecast followed by MILP cost minimization with a soil-moisture model built from literature coefficients. It was evaluated over 316 historical forecast origins and eight simulated operating scenarios, with no automated data link to a real installation and no digital twin wording.

R2220.ai_methods_detail: U-Net++ canopy segmentation, EfficientNet-B3 stress classification, CNN regressor for growth traits/LAI
R2220.justification: U-Net++, EfficientNet-B3 and a CNN regressor assess plant vigor from images and drive real-time shading and irrigation control, but these are image-based sensing and classification rather than a model of system behavior. The only system-behavior modelling is the 'simulated, yet realistic' yield, evaporation and PV-yield results, which have no stated automated link to the installation, and the work ran as greenhouse experiments.

R2591.ai_methods_detail: PV-geometry-conditioned shadow normalization (appearance canonization) network using array layout and sun-angle priors; federated prototype-based contrastive stress learner; secure aggregation with differential-privacy-style gradient perturbation and clipping; recognition and segmentation networks
R2591.justification: PrivAgriVolt is a federated deep-learning vision framework for crop-stress recognition that feeds physical PV-geometry and sun-angle priors into a shadow-normalization network. It was evaluated offline on vision benchmarks and has no virtual model of the agrivoltaic installation (hence NA). It is designed to run across farm clients with secure server aggregation.

R2171.justification: The abstract calls the outdoor agrivoltaic vertical farm 'fully automated, and AI-controlled' but names no ML, DL or RL method. It describes no virtual model of the system, only design features (3D-printed clay structure, crop selection, solar panels), so AI is a label and DT maturity is NA.

R2264.ai_methods_detail: Multiple linear regression and tree-based ensemble models (unspecified, e.g., random forest/boosting) on a meta-dataset of 546 observations
R2264.justification: This is a meta-analysis of 546 yield observations from 66 studies, analysed with multiple linear regression and 'tree-based ensemble models' (classical ML) to characterise yield responses to shading. It is an offline empirical analysis with no virtual model of a physical installation and no deployed system.

R1449.ai_methods_detail: k-medoids clustering (MATLAB, elbow method for k) to group ground insolation profiles; unsupervised classical ML used only for scenario reduction
R1449.justification: The study runs a geometric shading/insolation model on TMY data, applies k-medoids clustering to the 1620 insolation profiles (a borderline AI case: unsupervised clustering used for scenario reduction, not a predictive learner), then feeds the clusters to GrassGro and SAM to choose an optimal layout from 81, with no data link to a real installation and no digital twin wording.

R2470.ai_methods_detail: COCO-pretrained YOLOv8 (Ultralytics) for apple detection, applied without fine-tuning; SIFT coregistration and rule-based HSV red-pixel colour analysis; Mann-Whitney U and Fisher tests
R2470.justification: IoT cameras sent one image a day to the FieldClimate cloud, and the images were later analysed on a local i5/GTX 970 workstation with a pretrained YOLOv8 detector and HSV colour rules; this is a sensing and monitoring workflow with no virtual model of the orchard or the PV system, and it has no digital twin label.

R2625.ai_methods_detail: LSTM-Attention (main model), compared with standard LSTM, LSTM-GRU, BP neural network and SVM; Pearson correlation for feature selection
R2625.justification: A data-driven LSTM-Attention model built in Python/TensorFlow was trained and validated offline on a year of logged 10-minute sensor data to predict solar radiation and air temperature under three PV densities; there is no automated live data link and no actuation, and the authors do not use the digital twin term.

R0838.ai_methods_detail: CNN (TensorFlow, Adam optimizer) for tomato leaf disease classification from PiCam images; actuators controlled by threshold rules
R0838.justification: A small Raspberry Pi greenhouse prototype streams sensor data to a Blynk cloud dashboard, switches the fan, heater, LEDs and pump on threshold rules, runs solar tracking and classifies leaf disease with a CNN; it is an IoT sensing and control system with no virtual model of the system, so maturity is NA, and only qualitative evidence of the working prototype is reported.

R1692.ai_methods_detail: U-Net fully convolutional surrogate trained with combined L1 and adversarial (GAN discriminator) loss on Radiance/Accelerad raytracing outputs; k-means clustering to sample weather data
R1692.justification: A physics-informed U-Net/GAN surrogate trained on raytracer simulations predicts ground irradiance maps in 3 ms on a GPU, and the authors pitch it for on-the-fly edge PV tracker use; tests were offline on 2021 weather data, with no live data link to or control of the Morschenich-Alt system, and the digital twin term is not used.

R0022.exclusion_reason: The truncated abstract reads as an overview of IoAT-related agrivoltaic methods; it reports no developed system, data or results.

R2657.justification: The abstract describes a 'physics-informed explainable artificial intelligence' framework that combines analytical solar geometry and hourly PVsyst simulation with SHAP-based feature attribution, which implies a data-driven model, for the design of a 1.224 MWp vertical bifacial agrivoltaic system in Bangladesh. It is never called a digital twin and has no automated data link to a real installation, so it is an offline digital model used to predict and explain light stability (only the title and abstract were available).

R1387.ai_methods_detail: Transformer, Informer, Pyraformer, TimesNet (transformer-based time-series forecasting models)
R1387.justification: The abstract says it 'proposes models of irradiance time series prediction such as Pyraformer, Informer, Transformer and TimesNet', which were tested on historical PV-greenhouse weather and irradiance datasets. R1468.justification: The abstract presents 'a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model developed to predict PAR', trained on experimental data from two agrivoltaic greenhouses at the University of Jaén. R2066.ai_methods_detail: VMD_IMF12-Informer-BiLSTM (variational mode decomposition combined with Informer transformer and bidirectional LSTM), benchmarked against 8 other prediction methods
R2066.justification: The abstract proposes 'a novel region-specific VMD_IMF12-Informer-BiLSTM prediction model' for ultra-short-term PV greenhouse power, validated across prediction durations, seasons and input configurations with repeated experiments. It describes no digital twin, automated data link or live deployment, so this is an offline deep-learning forecasting model (digital_model).

R2262.ai_methods_detail: Kriging (Gaussian process) surrogate models of ray-tracing/physics PV and APSIM soybean simulations, with NSGA-II multi-objective optimization
R2262.justification: The abstract describes 'a coupled workflow integrating ray-tracing ground irradiance, a physics-based PV-energy model, an APSIM soybean model, Kriging surrogates, and NSGA-II optimization of PV tilt, mounting height, and row spacing'. Because Kriging is a Gaussian-process ML surrogate trained to emulate physics simulators, this counts as AI use. The model was checked against a pilot but has no automated data link, so it is an offline design-screening digital_model.

R0845.ai_methods_detail: Artificial neural network (ANN) combined with genetic algorithm (GA)
R0845.justification: The abstract discusses 'the application of artificial neural network and genetic algorithm to an experimental 0.675 kWp agrivoltaic system with turmeric crops'. R1894.ai_methods_detail: MLP, CNN, ResNet (deep learning) for residual heat prediction

R2381.ai_methods_detail: Stacked ensemble of XGBoost and CatBoost (gradient boosting), SHAP for interpretability

R2547.ai_methods_detail: Unspecified machine learning techniques for forecasting PV generation and water availability from GCM outputs (algorithms not named in abstract); NSGA-II for multi-objective optimization (not AI)

R2598.ai_methods_detail: Dual attention mechanism-based quantum LSTM (DAM-QLSTM) for forecasting; variational quantum circuit (VQC) based rolling optimization for scheduling
R2598.justification: The study develops a quantum LSTM with dual attention (DAM-QLSTM) to forecast supply and demand, then a VQC-based rolling optimization with multi-physics constraints for scheduling, 'validated using practical data from a PV greenhouse in Beijing'; it never uses the term digital twin and describes no automated live data flow or commands sent to the greenhouse, so this is a digital model checked offline on recorded data.

R1354.ai_methods_detail: CNN-BiGRU-Attention hybrid deep learning model tuned with the TTAO metaheuristic optimizer; benchmarked against 9 comparison models
R1354.justification: The study proposes a 'TTAO-CNN-BiGRU-Attention framework' to forecast ultra-short-term irradiance in a PV greenhouse and uses statistical methods to analyse monthly and seasonal patterns; it evaluates the model offline across data volumes and seasons, with no digital twin term and no automated link to the greenhouse.

R1108.justification: The abstract reports only a technical and economic feasibility analysis of putting a photovoltaic device on a greenhouse, and it describes no physics-based or data-driven model of the installation's behavior, no data link and no actuation. R0803.justification: Production data were taken from the PV providers' web platforms and compared by hand with the theoretical annual production of each greenhouse estimated with the Solar Explorer web tool. R1105.justification: The study runs simulations and experiments on single-axis bifacial trackers using fixed strategies (maximum power and minimum shadow area) and a seasonal mode switch, so a model of the energy and shading behavior exists. R2900.justification: Microclimate data logged every 15 minutes and daily yield data from an Italian agrivoltaic field were analysed after the fact with PCA and K-means clustering (classical machine learning). The study is a data analysis with no system implemented, so the status is NA.

R1084.justification: Plant growth and microclimate (air and substrate temperature, substrate moisture) were measured in a replicated trial under a fixed PV array on a simulated rooftop, and light conditions were modeled, which is a light-subsystem virtual model with no automated data link from the installation. R1623.justification: The study uses an analytical solar-geometry model of the light and energy subsystem to compute tracking efficiency for E-W, N-S and latitude-inclined axes, panel inclination and a 3.79 m array spacing for a generic design at 50 degrees latitude, with no data link to any installation. R0909.justification: The Piolenc trial used a fixed afternoon-shading steering policy, and ETo was computed post hoc. Final check: the closed loop is a design evaluated only conceptually, so the implementation status of the twin is concept or proposal; the field trial ran a fixed shading policy.
